# Flying Cheep Cheep reference

Captured from the established Super Mario Bros. (U) ROM in headless Mesen on 2026-11-18. SHA-256 `f61548fdf1670cffefcc4f0b7bdcdd9eaba0c226e3b74f8666071496988248de`.

These controlled RAM fixtures let the original ROM run movement and contact after setup. They are not continuous playthroughs. Flight fixtures start at NES Y248, horizontal speed +/-2 px/tick, Y speed -5 and zero fractions. The geometry includes solid bridge rows. Far-side fixtures begin at X600/-128, Y80 and zero velocity. Fraction fixtures begin at (80,248), speed (1.75,-5), with fractions (0,0) or (127,208). Their initial spawn-only row is omitted.

Stomp fixtures begin at enemy (128,160), velocity zero and zero fractions. Mario's post-movement origin is (128,145) for descending contact, (128,144) when stationary, and (128,143) when rising. The player's speed fraction is 144 at contact. Fireball contact starts at enemy (152,184), speed fraction 68 and position fraction 78. Starman starts at (128,148), or (128,17) for the above-camera knockout. The shell fixture hits after the fish has moved, with speed fraction 68 and position fraction 78. It holds the hit pose and begins knockout motion next tick. Defeat traces include the hit tick. Points are decoded to full score values. The flip column is read from NES OAM attributes.

CSV data is deliberately excluded from Godot imports with this folder's `.gdignore`. Tests read it with FileAccess.

`spawn_mesen.csv` records 28 controlled initializer cases: stationary, walking, running, leftward movement, both speed thresholds, all four seed bits and cooldown selections. Mario's NES X is 128. The ROM performs the initializer after the random bytes are supplied; expected spawn coordinates, speed and cooldown come from Mesen.

`stream_normal_mesen.csv` contains 2,027 ticks with the camera advancing at 1.5 px/tick; `stream_fast_mesen.csv` contains 1,257 ticks at 2.5 px/tick after its first two ticks. Both were rerun in headless Mesen on 2026-11-18. Mario holds Right and Run with his position held above terrain to avoid contacts and coin VRAM updates. `stream_halfway_mesen.csv` contains 181 ticks after a real timeout death and halfway restart, with NES Y held at zero. The original ROM runs camera scrolling, map parsing, launch selection, enemy motion and cleanup. These are controlled route probes, not normal playthrough recordings.

The route fixtures include all five slot flags and the ordinary gray Cheep Cheep spawned by `$0F,$8A` at `E_GroundArea8 + 16`. In the fast route it takes slot 0 at end frame 1109, camera X2002, retaining fractions (192,196), and releases on frame 1246. The 137 occupied samples remain at Y248 and move left by 1/4 px/tick. In the normal route it takes slot 3 at frame 1661, camera X2001, with zero fractions and a downward bob flag. Its 65 occupied samples end at NES Y256 before the next draw step clears it. The fixtures record its origin, fractions, bob flag and random byte, rather than prescribing its lifetime to the implementation.

The Godot test replays the captured camera/player positions and native random bytes. It compares every parsed column, graphics task, queued command, frenzy state, cooldown, slot flag, spawn position, speed and retained fraction, plus each occupied hidden-fish pose. It runs all three datasets in the sandbox and actual 2-3 scene for 6,930 route comparisons. This checks native selection rules with identical inputs, without claiming that Godot and the NES share an uncontrolled global random sequence. The runtime random source is unchanged by the facing/lifecycle fix.

Source routines: `AreaFrenzy`, `ChkEnemyFrenzy`, `InitFlyingCheepCheep`, `MoveFlyingCheepCheep`, and `EraseEnemyObject`. The actor's final retirement keeps the horizontal fraction produced by the ROM's fall-through horizontal update. Callback spawn rows are aligned with the following end-frame sample.

`facing_hits_mesen.csv` records the upright hit-frame and following defeated OAM attributes for both flight directions and both sides of Mario. It comes from four fresh Starman contact probes. The atlas is horizontally mirrored relative to native CHR art, so native OAM H-flip corresponds to an unflipped Godot sprite. Tests also exercise the same shared pose handoff through stomp and fireball entry points. Starman and stomp hold the old facing for the hit frame; fireballs reveal the corrected facing immediately. Movement and scoring are unchanged.
